transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because I just can't stop seeing this... this droop and unevenness around my mouth and jaw. It's all I can look at in every single photo and reflection. People keep telling me I look fine, but it feels so incredibly obvious to me. It's gotten to the point where it's really affecting my work. I've actually started avoiding presentations and meeting with clients because I just can't handle them looking at it.
Is it only your mouth and jaw area that you're concerned about, or are there other parts of your body that you also focus on?
No, it's really just my mouth and jaw area. I mean, I don't focus on anything else the way I do with this. It's specifically the lower half of my face that's the problem.
How much distress would you say this concern about your mouth and jaw area is causing you?
I don't know exactly how to measure it, but... it's a lot. It's really severe. It just constantly weighs on me, and I feel pretty miserable about it most of the time. It's just very overwhelming.
Have you avoided any social interactions because of your concern about your mouth and jaw area?

Yes, quite a lot, actually. I... I recently cancelled a major client presentation right at the last minute because I just couldn't face being seen by everyone. And I've been missing these award-related networking events for my work, too. It's just getting too hard to be out in front of people. 

Honestly, everything is starting to fall apart around this. My project deadlines are slipping, and I'm even skipping family gatherings now. I just don't want anyone looking at my face.
Do you believe your mouth and jaw area actually look uneven and droopy to others, or is it just that you feel like they should look different?

I believe it actually looks that way. I mean... people will sometimes tell me I look fine, but I just don't see how that's possible. I can't stop seeing this droop and unevenness around my mouth and jaw in every single photo and every reflection. 

It feels so obvious. That's really why I'm here... because it's so glaring to me that, like I said, I've started avoiding my clients and those presentations. Even if people say they don't notice it, it's just too obvious for me to ignore.
Have you ever had a time when you didn't think your mouth and jaw area looked uneven and droopy?
No, not really. I mean, it feels like it's always been this way. I can't remember a time when I looked in the mirror and didn't see it. It's just... always been there, looking uneven and droopy.
Does your perception of the unevenness and droopiness around your mouth and jaw area ever change, or is it always the same?

It's pretty much always the same. I don't... I don't really have days where it looks any better to me. Every time I look, it's just right there, exactly as bad as it always is. It's just a constant thing.
Have you tried to do anything to fix or improve the appearance of your mouth and jaw area?

Well, I do a lot to try and hide it, or at least figure out how bad it is. Before I go to work or... or any family event, really, I can spend hours in the bathroom. I'll check the mirror constantly, and I take pictures on my phone from all these different angles to see how the droop looks. 

I end up redoing my makeup over and over, trying to contour it away, and I always wear a scarf to try and cover the jawline. I'm always asking my husband if my face looks lopsided, which I know frustrates him. And then... I just sit there scrolling through pictures of other women online, just comparing their faces to mine to see how much worse I look. It just takes up so much time.
Have you noticed any significant impact on your relationships with family or friends due to your concerns about your mouth and jaw area?

Yes, it really has. Family gatherings have just started to fall apart because of this. I just... I can't face being seen by anyone. 

And it's not just with my family and friends, it's heavily affecting my work, too. I actually cancelled a major client presentation at the very last minute recently. I've also been missing out on all this award-related networking because I just can't stand the thought of people looking at my face. Because I'm hiding away so much, my project deadlines are falling apart right along with the family events. It's just impacting everything.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your mouth and jaw area might not look as uneven and droopy as you think they do?

I... I hear what you're saying, and I know people tell me I look fine, but no. I can't really believe that. I'm here because I just can't stop seeing this droop and the unevenness around my mouth and jaw. It's in every photo, every reflection. Even when my husband or someone else says they don't see it, it just feels so incredibly obvious to me. It's so real to me that, like I said, I've started avoiding my presentations and my clients. I just can't see it any other way.
Do you think you would be satisfied with your appearance if your mouth and jaw area looked perfectly even and not droopy?

I don't know. I mean, maybe? If it was perfectly even, I guess I wouldn't have to worry about this specific problem anymore. But honestly, it's hard to imagine what that would even feel like right now. I just know how much this bothers me, so if it was fixed, I suppose I'd be happier. But I'm not really sure if I'd be completely satisfied with everything else. I just want this part to not look so awful.
Have you ever had concerns about other parts of your body besides your mouth and jaw area?

No, not really. I mean, I don't think so. It's really just my mouth and my jaw area. That's the only thing that I... well, that's what takes up all my attention. I haven't really focused on or worried about any other part of my body, just the lower half of my face.
Do you think there's any possibility that your perception of your mouth and jaw area is not accurate?

I don't think so. I mean, I know what I see. I look in the mirror every day, and it's right there. The unevenness, the way it droops... it's just so clear to me. I understand that maybe other people don't notice it as much, or they're just being polite, but to me, it's very real. I don't see how my perception could be wrong when it's just so obvious every time I look at my face.
Have you ever had a period where your concerns about your mouth and jaw area lessened or went away, even if only for a short time?

No, I really haven't. It's... it's always there. I can't remember a time in recent years where I didn't feel this way about it. It just constantly bothers me, day in and day out. There hasn't been any break from it.
Have you ever seen a dermatologist or plastic surgeon about the appearance of your mouth and jaw area?
No, I haven't. I mean, I've definitely thought about it... a lot. But I haven't actually made an appointment or gone to see a plastic surgeon or anyone like that yet.
